newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Nov manufacturers' shipments rise 3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Nov manufacturers' shipments rise 3.0 pct.

text.p: Canadian manufacturers' shipments rose 3.0 percent in November, to C$34.28 billion seasonally adjusted from a revised C$33.30 (C$33.24) billion in October, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast shipments to rise 2.8 percent, unfilled orders to fall 0.6 percent, new orders to rise 0.5 percent and an inventory/shipment ratio of 1.33.

Statistics Canada said the total increase in manufacturing shipments was due mostly to a resurgence in the automotive sector which had lost some momentum due to the October strike at General Motors Corp's Canadian unit.
"After a lackluster 1995, the pattern of halting growth seen in shipments in mid-1996 appears to have flattened out in recent months," the agency said.

The November increase in inventories was the largest of four consecutive months of gains, "just shy" of the all-time high set in November 1995. The largest increase came from the aircraft and parts industry. The wood, chemical products and electrical and electronic products sectors also posted gains.
Manufacturers' backlog of unfilled orders, a key indicator of future shipments, declined for the third month in a row in November.
